g.text: SKILL 4 OF 5 · §2.4 PAPER2BLOG
Paper2Blog writes the Chinese and English articles separately from one
evidence map, then gates the Word files on layout
Figure 7: assets → evidence map → multilingual drafts → editorial QA loop → the Chinese and English DOCX (§2.4)
FIG. 7
ROOT DELIVERABLES
The Chinese article, cast as a WeChat public-account piece
The English article, cast as a research-blog piece
Same facts, figures, numbers, claims, and source links; different openings,
pacing, and examples; outlines, previews, and QA reports stay in the
intermediates directory

Package gate: both DOCX exist and are readable, contain enough article text, embed images rather than link them, carry no placeholder text, declare a Latin body font and a Chinese fallback; embedded image count,
identity, and order are compared across the two languages, extracted numeric claims and technical-looking terms are cross-checked — concrete divergences, not writing style.

g.text: ID
Requirement
Solution the paper gives
C1
One evidence base for two languages — the articles may differ in
pacing but cannot drift on results, method names, figures, or links
One evidence map from the bundle: hook, problem, method components, claims, quantitative results, limitations, links, figure roles; a
missing hard fact (code link, DOI, venue, affiliation) is omitted, never guessed
C2
Register must be controlled during writing — a deterministic script
cannot check it afterwards
The two articles are written separately from language-specific outlines and a style guide (restrained public-account register vs neutral
research blog), not translated sentence by sentence
C3
Figures need article-level selection and placement
A small shared figure set, the same in both languages, each placed next to the section that prepares the reader, with captions per language;
readability after DOCX resizing is checked
C4
The deliverable is a Word article, not plain text
Fixed filenames, embedded media, captions in the matching language, source links, editor-friendly fonts (Latin body font plus a Chinese
fallback)
C5
Word layout has to be editor-ready — blank pages, thumbnails,
orphan tails
Underfilled images, images pushed to the next page, and orphan tails are read from the document structure; strict mode renders page
images to catch near-blank pages and bottom whitespace
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)
